ITEM 1  CEREMONIAL/PRESENTATIONS

  A. Planning Commission Reorganization
  Recommended Action: Conduct the Election ofChair and Vice Chair as
  needed.
  Staff Contact: Senior Management Analyst Evans, 456—2489, ext. 246

  Vice Chair Peak opened nominations for Chair.

  Commissioner Leonard nominated Vice Chair Peak; Commissioner Mazza
  nominated himself; and Commissioner Riddick nominated Vice Chair Peak.

  The question was called and Vice Chair Peak was elected Chair 3—1 a
  Commissioner Mazza dissenting.

  Chair Peak opened nominations for Vice Chair.

  Commissioner Leonard nominated himself and Commissioner Mazza
  nominated himself for the position ofVice Chair.

  The question was called and Commissioner Leonard was elected Vice Chair,
  3-1. Commissioner Mazza dissenting.

  Commissioner Riddick administered the Oath of Offlce to the newly elected
  Chair and Vice Chair.

ITEM 2.A.  PUBLIC COMMENTS

  Rob MacLeod proposed a plan for the long-term Viability of Pacific Coast
  Highway (PCH) through the Palisades burn scar. widening PCH landward and
  benefltting approximately 309 private beachfront rebuild property owners. Most
  beachfront homes which were supported by caissons lost structural stability in the
  2000-degree heat from the Palisades Fire. Those impacted in this way should opt
  in for debris removal as soon as possible to avoid further damage to the ocean and
  he asked the Public Works Director to inform property owners of this as soon as
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes OfMarch 17” 2025
  Page 3 0f9

  possiblé. He also advocated for extension of sewer lines to those properties rather
  than replacement ofonsite wastewater treatment systems.

ITEM 2.B.  COMMISSION / STAFF COMMENTS

  Interim Planning Director Tamuri provided a brief Planning Rebuild Update. The
  rebuild code amendments were passed by City Council as Emergency Ordinance
  No. 524U for Malibu Municipal Code Zoning Text Amendment No. 25-001 (to
  benefit those impacted by the Woolsey, Broad and Franklin Fires) and Local
  Coastal Program Amendment No. 25-001 (primarily for those impacted by the
  Palisades Fire) as Ordinance No. 524. The Local Coastal Program Amendment
  was pending California Coastal Commission approval during their meeting on
  April 9, 10 or ll, 2025 to be held in Santa Barbara. Two Planning Verification-
  Palisades Fire applications were approved and six additional Planning
  Verification applications were submitted and in progress. The Rebuild Center
  staff assisted 86 people in the first week of operation. An open house was
  scheduled for March 19m, 5:00 to 7:00 p.m. at 23805 Stuart Ranch Road. 143 of
  the 307 Public Records Requests filed were completed. The City Council planned
  a series of special work sessions related to the fire rebuilds. On March 18m a
  community meeting regarding beachfront properties would be held at City Hall
  and via Zoom at 4:00 p.m.; on March 19‘“ a special City Council meeting focused
  on fire rebuild policy was scheduled to begin at 1:00 p.m. Additional upcoming
  meetings would focus on neighborhoods beginning with Big Rock and Calle de
  Barco Assessment Districts then Rambla Pacifico, La Costa, Las Flores, Pena
  Road, and 20727 to 20759 PCH.

  Interim Planning Director Tamuri also noted upcoming town hall meetings with
  Southern California Edison’s project to underground powerlines in the Nicholas
  Circuit on March 20m at 5:00 p.m. at City Hall and via Zoom and an April 2“d
  town hall with the California Department of Insurance at 4:00 p.m. at City Hall
  and via Zoom. The Malibu Rebuilds website, https://maliburebuilds.org/, would
  be regularly updated with future meetings added to the News. Events and
  Deadlines webpage.

  Commissioner Mazza asked who was in charge ofthe Rebuild Center.

  ln response to Commissioner Mazza. Interim Planning Director Tamuri noted the
  Rebuild Center was under the administration of the City Manager‘s Office.

  Commissioner Riddick asked for the hearing for the emergency tower at Bluffs
  Park to be brought to the Commission as soon as possible. She expressed
  appreciation for public input on proposed developments.
   Malibu Planning Commission
  Minutes ofMarch 17. 2025
  Page 4 of 9

  Commissioner Mazza suggested Mr. MacLeod‘s publish his submitted
  correspondence as it dealt with planning to keep PCH open in the future. He
  thanked former Chair Hill for his service to the community and his detailed work
  with project review. He asked that the meeting that evening be dedicated to Kraig
  Hill.

  Commissioner Leonard attended several of the fire rebuild workshops and
  suggested residents view or participate in them. He thanked stafffor their efforts.
  Commissioner Leonard met with Big Rock residents and shared his prior
  experiences with fire rebuilds.

CONSENSUS Chair Peak thanked Commissioner Mazza for his comments regarding former
  Chair Hill‘s service and the Commission agreed to dedicate the meeting in his
  honor by unanimous consensus.

  Assistant City Attorney Martz noted that March 3], 2025 was the deadline to
  either opt in or opt out for Phase l debris removal.
